contents.name: Partial trace, reduced state, and coordinate contraction (2.30)–(2.34)

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete definition of reduction as a partial trace, its trace characterization, and the coordinate formula in §2.1.3.
source_review.supports: The ordered finite-factor contraction formula and the meaning of the reduced outside operator.
source_review.limitations: The assigned item proves positivity, trace preservation, uniqueness, and basis independence itself for arbitrary mixed finite densities; no continuum factorization is imported.

contents.name: Example 2.8: a reduced maximally mixed state (2.35)–(2.37)

source_review.read_extent: Read the full finite entangled-vector calculation and its reduced state I/|Σ|.
source_review.supports: A finite partial trace can produce a maximally mixed output; the assigned N-qubit spectrum and growth are calculated locally.
source_review.limitations: The example does not state a cutoff-limit growth theorem and supplies no field-theoretic divergence law.

source_review.read_extent: Read the explicit statement that Watrous writes log for base 2 and ln for the natural logarithm.

contents.name: Definition 5.17: finite spectral von Neumann entropy and zero-eigenvalue convention

source_review.read_extent: Read the full finite positive-semidefinite-operator entropy definition and its spectral expression.
source_review.supports: Entropy as a finite spectral sum, including the zero-eigenvalue case.
source_review.limitations: Watrous uses its stated base-2 information convention; the local item uses natural logarithms and k_B exactly as specified by its mathematical supplier and plan.

contents.name: Definition 5.18: finite support-sensitive relative entropy
contents.reason: No relative entropy, support comparison, mixing inequality, product additivity, or subadditivity is asserted or used in the finite-regulator items.

contents.name: Partial trace and reduced density operator (2.63)–(2.67)

source_review.read_extent: Read the bipartite partial-trace formula, its action on a basis, and the equality with reduced-state expectation values.
source_review.supports: The finite-factor reduced-density construction and factor ordering.
source_review.limitations: The displayed worked derivation starts from a pure bipartite state; the assigned result covers arbitrary mixed inputs by a separate local matrix proof.

contents.name: Positivity and unit trace checks for the displayed pure-state reduction
contents.reason: The notes verify these properties for the displayed pure bipartite vector; the assigned definition proves them for every finite mixed density operator without relying on this narrower calculation.

contents.name: Equations (10.59)–(10.61): entropy from the eigenvalue distribution

source_review.read_extent: Read the density-operator entropy formula, diagonal spectral expansion, and identification with entropy of the eigenvalue vector.
source_review.supports: The finite spectral form used in the definition and the maximally mixed cutoff calculation.
source_review.limitations: The surrounding treatment uses information measured in bits by default; the item explicitly uses natural logarithms and the k_B scale.

contents.name: Pure-state density has zero entropy (first property in §10.2.1)
contents.reason: The example calculates the pure qubit entropy directly from its eigenvalues, so it does not rely on this general property.

contents.name: Unitary invariance of finite von Neumann entropy (second property in §10.2.1)
contents.reason: No unitary transformation or change of state is used in the assigned cutoff or two-matrix calculations.

contents.name: Maximum entropy at uniform spectrum (third property in §10.2.1)
contents.reason: The cutoff calculation proves its uniform-spectrum value by summing eigenvalues directly and does not invoke a maximum principle.
